slides.title: 4 p*rn relapse traps waiting [[on the final weekend of No Nut November.]]
slides.sub: 5 days left. Don't hand it away on Saturday.

slides.title: "Celebrating" [[early]]
slides.body: Drinks on Friday, guard down by midnight. Alcohol plus a phone in bed is a classic p*rn relapse.

slides.title: [[Lazy]] Saturday
slides.body: No plans, all day in your room. Empty weekends are where streaks go to die.

slides.title: Traps [[3–4]]
items: "Testing" yourself — just a peek to prove you're fine.
Sunday-night dread — stress about Monday goes looking for p*rn.

slides.title: Lock the [[weekend]]
items: Plan Friday night — with people, home by midnight.
Book Saturday morning — gym, game, anything.
No tests. You've proved enough.
Sunday: plan the week by 8 PM, phone off by 11.

carousels.name: 6 habits that keep you out of the 42% watching p*rn almost daily

slides.title: 6 habits that keep you out of the 42% [[watching p*rn almost daily.]]
slides.sub: 42% of men 18–29 watch daily or several times a week.

slides.title: Daily or [[almost]]
slides.body: An Institute for Family Studies / YouGov survey of 2,000 young men (2026) found 42% of men aged 18–29 watch p*rn daily or several times a week.

slides.title: Habits [[1–3]]
items: Phone out of the bedroom at night.
A plan for the evening before it starts.
Real friends you see in person every week.

slides.title: Habits [[4–6]]
items: Training 3+ times a week.
A goal bigger than the weekend.
Someone who knows you're quitting p*rn.

slides.title: Start with [[one]]
items: Pick the easiest habit for you.
Do it for 7 days straight.
Add a second next week.
Track your p*rn-free days alongside it.

carousels.name: 4 reasons arguments end in p*rn and how to break the pattern

slides.title: 4 reasons arguments end in p*rn [[— and how to break the pattern.]]
You want [[control]]
slides.body: An argument makes you feel powerless. P*rn feels like something you control. It isn't.

slides.title: You want to [[numb]] it
slides.body: Anger and hurt feel too big. P*rn turns the volume down — for 10 minutes.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–4]]
items: You want to disappear — no talking, no fixing.
Revenge thinking: "They don't care, so why should I?"

slides.title: Next time, [[instead]]
items: Leave the room, not the relationship — go for a walk.
Move hard for 10 minutes.
Write what you wanted to say, then wait.
Come back and repair once you're calm.

carousels.name: 6 escape spots when a craving catches you at home

slides.title: 6 escape spots [[when a p*rn craving catches you at home.]]
slides.sub: Change the place. Change the outcome.

slides.title: Go [[1–3]]
items: Outside — even the balcony or front step.
The gym — urges often fade mid-workout.
A café — people around, phone stays honest.

slides.title: Go [[4–6]]
items: The library — quiet, public, no privacy for p*rn.
A friend's place — text first, then show up.
A walking route you've planned in advance.

slides.title: Why it [[works]]
slides.body: Many p*rn urges need two things: privacy and a screen. Take away the privacy and the urge loses its grip.

slides.title: Set it up [[now]]
items: Pick your top 2 places.
Keep shoes and keys by the door.
Leave within 2 minutes of the urge.
Stay out 20 minutes before deciding anything.

carousels.name: 5 promises about p*rn to make before NNN ends

slides.title: 5 promises about p*rn to make yourself [[before No Nut November ends.]]
Promises [[1–2]]
items: "I won't hide it" — if I slip, someone will know.
"I won't test myself" — no peeking to prove I'm fine.

slides.title: Promises [[3–4]]
items: "I'll protect my nights" — phone out, lights out.
"I'll ask for help" before it gets bad, not after.

slides.title: "I'll [[keep going]]"
slides.body: November ends. Quitting p*rn doesn't. The promise isn't 30 days. It's who you're becoming.

slides.title: Make them [[real]]
items: Write them down by hand.
Sign and date the page.
Tell one person your p*rn promises.
Read them on Day 30.
